subject.title: fix(cron): prevent double dispatch after disable/enable cycle during in-flight run

question: Should this PR intentionally preserve disabled jobs' fresh `runningAtMs` markers until completion or `STUCK_RUN_MS` so disable/re-enable cannot create a second concurrent dispatch?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and well-proven, but it changes persisted runtime-state semantics for disabled or re-enabled cron jobs after a crash or interrupted run; that owner acceptance is a merge-risk decision rather than an automatable repair.

options.title: Accept preserved-marker semantics
options.body: Land after cron owner and required CODEOWNERS review confirm the short-term blocked re-enable behavior is the right tradeoff for duplicate-run prevention.

options.title: Narrow to the active-registry guard
options.body: Remove the persisted disabled-marker preservation and rely only on in-process `isCronJobActive`, accepting weaker restart durability.

options.title: Pause for a scheduler lease design
options.body: Hold this PR if maintainers want a broader atomic claim or lease primitive instead of the focused fix.

recommendation.title: Accept preserved-marker semantics
recommendation.body: Land after cron owner and required CODEOWNERS review confirm the short-term blocked re-enable behavior is the right tradeoff for duplicate-run prevention.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has recent major cron scheduler changes and explicit maintainer status, making them the best available owner for the persisted-state tradeoff.
